messages:
incident-bot: Incident created: GPU OOM (prefill) on pool 'g4-large-context' — multiple container restarts observed. Pager sent to oncall.
ben_oncall: got pager, looking. Seeing repeated container restarts on node gpu-idx-17, OOM during prefill for requests with ~200k token context. CPU fine, GPU mem spikes then CUDA driver reports out-of-memory and container restarts.
alice_sre: confirmed logs on node: `CudaError: out of memory` followed by `SIGKILL` of container. Also seeing KV cache growth before restart. Dumping last 10 lines: ```[15:23:11] prefill_open: ctx_size=192512 tokens, kv_mem=14.3GB
[15:23:12] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[15:23:12] container: killed (OOM)``` 
charu_eng: that ctx_size number is huge — customers hitting extremely long context windows from one tenant (maria_cust_success: reference later). Is there a recent model change or a policy change that would allow that size?
ben_oncall: no model change in prod; traffic spike from a customer started ~15:20 UTC. I'm seeing repeated allocation attempts on same container; prefill path doesn't cap context length before allocation.
dave_platform: can we hotpatch a prefill-context cap in the runtime config? Even a soft cap (e.g., 64k) to avoid huge prefill allocations would buy time.
charu_eng: yes, we can toggle `prefill_max_context_tokens` via runtime feature flag. I can push a temporary cap to 65536 tokens for the pool. Will do now.
charu_eng: deploying feature-flag patch to pool 'g4-large-context' (rolling). Command: `redwoodctl runtime set-flag --pool g4-large-context --flag prefill_max_context_tokens=65536 --ttl 30m`
ben_oncall: applied. I'll tail node logs for immediate effect.
alice_sre: after flag push, observed allocation attempts drop; new prefill requests >65k tokens get rejected with `413 Payload Too Large` at the edge. That reduces pressure but we still have several nodes with fragmented GPU memory from previous allocations.
eva_support: customer impact? Maria, do we have which customer saw the 200k token requests?
maria_cust_success: yes — customer team 'LexiconAI' reported bulk ingestion job sending long transcripts. They confirmed they started a high-volume import at ~15:18 UTC. Customer says they can pause ingest.
maria_cust_success: notifying customer to pause ingestion and we asked for ETA to restart.
ben_oncall: spinning up replacement nodes in the pool and draining affected nodes. `autoscale` fired but we hit quota on a subset; requesting burst allocation from infra.
dave_platform: granted temporary burst quota +2 nodes. Provisioning now.
charu_eng: also enabling stripe-eviction mitigation on GPU runtime (experimental): this forces large KV stripes to be evicted to host memory earlier to avoid full OOM. Patch applied with `runtime set-param --pool g4-large-context gpu_eviction=striped_host_swap`
alice_sre: enabling stripe eviction shows gradual reduction in resident GPU memory per container. A few containers still OOM'ing during first subsequent prefill because of fragmented allocations.
ben_oncall: manually cordoned node gpu-idx-17 and restarted kubelet on it to clear orphaned GPU allocations.
incident-bot: NOTE: status page update suggested. Current status: Service degraded for long-context generation on g4-large-context pool. ETA mitigation: immediate soft cap + node replacements + stripe-eviction enabled. Next update in 15 minutes.
eva_support: sending customer-facing message: "We're mitigating a memory pressure issue affecting large-context requests. We've asked customers to pause high-volume imports and applied a temporary context limit. We'll follow up when nodes are fully healthy." :white_check_mark:
maria_cust_success: LexiconAI acknowledged and paused ingestion; they requested an incident summary and ETA to fully restore large-context capability.
charu_eng: next steps: 1) continue draining/replacing affected nodes 2) run GPU defragmentation (container restart + driver reset) on remaining nodes 3) revise prefill path to perform a cheap client-size check before heavy GPU allocation 4) schedule follow-up fix to stream prefill allocations instead of all-at-once.
ben_oncall: handoff to night oncall in 45m. I'll prepare a concise handoff note.
ben_oncall: Handoff note -> "Prefill OOM due to >100k token client requests -> soft cap 65k applied to pool; stripe-eviction enabled; 2 replacement nodes added; customer paused ingest; remaining nodes being drained and restarted. Monitoring GPU memory and container restarts. Contact oncall-night for follow-ups: @charu_eng and @alice_sre are primary engineers."
alice_sre: adding debugging snippet for post-incident RCA: ```# check OOM traces
kubectl logs -n runtime -l node=gpu-idx-17 --tail=200 | grep -i oom
# dump KV cache sizes
redwoodctl debug kvcache dump --node gpu-idx-17 --top 20
``` 
charu_eng: we should add a regression test exercising streaming prefill for >100k tokens in CI to avoid recurrence.
ben_oncall: leaving a reminder for status page: once all nodes show <5 restarts in 1h and queue length normal, mark resolved. For now, incident remains active.
incident-bot: Incident severity updated to Sev2 — partial customer impact: LexiconAI ingestion stalled, some other large-context calls were rate-limited. Page routed to oncall at 15:24 UTC.
maria_cust_success: will draft a customer incident note and include expected timeline for re-enabling >65k contexts after deeper fixes. Sharing draft in #customer-updates shortly.
charu_eng: tagging follow-ups: - runtime: implement prefill stream allocation (PR in progress) - platform: add automated stripe-eviction toggle to autoscaler - docs: update guidance for customers about recommended max ingest chunk size.
ben_oncall: thanks everyone. I'll finalize handoff and keep watch during the rotation. If anything regresses ping me directly. :thumbsup:
